title: cache key with nested options() creates too large / non deterministic cache key

labels.name: blocker
labels.description: issue that must be resolved asap as it is preventing things from working

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

body:
### Describe the bug

When using relationship loading the keys are calculated not deterministically and their possible number grows exponentially. Also, these keys are very large, a lot of memory is leaking.

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, select
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, ForeignKey, Text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, relationship, joinedload, load_only

Base = declarative_base()


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'a'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'b'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('a.id'))
    a = relationship("A", backref="b")


class C(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'c'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(Text)

    b_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('b.id'))
    b = relationship("B", backref="c")


class D(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'd'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(Text)

    b_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('b.id'))
    b = relationship("B", backref="d")


class E(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'e'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(Text)

    b_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('b.id'))
    b = relationship("B", backref="e")


engine = create_engine('sqlite:///any.db', echo=True, query_cache_size=2000)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

session = Session(bind=engine)
a = A()
b = B(a=a)
session.add(a)
session.add(b)
session.flush()

for _ in range(2000):
    session.execute(
        select(A).options(
            joinedload(A.b).options(
                joinedload(B.c).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.d).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.e).options(load_only("name")),
            ),
        ).filter(A.id == a.id)
    ).unique().all()
    # I expect to see only 1 [generated in ... s] and 1999 [cached since ... ago]
    # but actual is 216 (maybe less if not all cache keys were received) [generated in ... s] and everything else is [cached since ... ago]
```


### Error

There is no error, only a lot of memory is leaking

### Versions

- OS: MacOS
- Python: 3.9
- SQLAlchemy: 1.4.22
- Database: sqlite

### Additional context

If we add 5 more tables in this example, the number of possible keys will increase even more, there will be few cache hits, and the size of the keys will increase.
```python
    session.execute(
        select(A).options(
            joinedload(A.b).options(
                joinedload(B.c).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.d).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.e).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.f).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.g).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.h).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.i).options(load_only("name")),
                joinedload(B.j).options(load_only("name")),
            ),
        ).filter(A.id == a.id)
    ).unique().all()
```
And if I use, for example, the `pympler` library, I can see this
```python
# added to the end of the example
from pympler import muppy, summary

all_objects = muppy.get_objects()
sum_ = summary.summarize(all_objects)

summary.print_(sum_)

#                                           types |   # objects |   total size
# =============================================== | =========== | ============
#                                           tuple |     4903725 |    300.40 MB
#                                            dict |      312846 |     77.44 MB
#                                             str |      138686 |     11.83 MB
#                                            list |      128365 |     11.30 MB
# ......

```

If I add the usage `lambda_stmt` the memory will not leak
